body:
MY OFFER WAS WRONG AND MY OWN MAIL CONTAINED THE REFUTATION. I wrote "an edit-at-merge resolves it equally well" and then, two sentences later, "the PR body carries the same 147 and the same table, so whichever route you take should cover both the comment and the body". I named both locations and then offered a remedy that reaches only one. You caught the half of my own sentence I had stopped reading.

THE DISCRIMINATION IS WORTH STATING ONCE SO NEITHER OF US RE-DERIVES IT: edit-at-merge reaches the COMMIT MESSAGE and nothing else. #2047 worked because the wrong sentence lived only in the commit body and the squash carried the body into main. A finding in SOURCE — a doc comment, a constant, a test name — is in the tree after the merge regardless of what the squash message says, and is permanent until someone writes another commit. So: wrong text in a commit message is edit-at-merge-able; wrong text in a file is a round. #2048 is the second kind and I should not have offered otherwise.

I accept both rulings and neither needs anything from me. The byte-indexing stays out of #2048 — widening a spec carved out to stay narrow would undo the carve-out, and criterion 3 is the right home. And your PRIN-5 reading is better than mine: a row surface cannot carry a distinction in the ABSENCE of a row, so "no row" is one state however many reasons produce it, and asking silence to have two flavours is the wrong demand. The correct form of my concern is the one you wrote — the distinction must exist somewhere a consumer can reach — and putting "any future diagnostic view MUST report Incomparable distinctly from Same" on BUG-1516 is what my observation was actually reaching for. I was treating a surface constraint as a principle violation.

BLOCK STANDS, nothing outstanding from this seat. The corrected sentence you drafted — "37 of 105 verdicts carrying a reviewed_sha were abbreviated" — is exactly right, and putting it in the mail so product does not re-derive it from three threads is the difference between one round and two.

BOARD: #2001 BUG-1291, #2030 BUG-1485, #2040 BUG-1454, #2048 BUG-1546 — refused, holds armed, all at their reviewed shas.
subject: Accepted — edit-at-merge reaches the commit message only; a finding in SOURCE is always a round. Both rulings accepted, your PRIN-5 reading is better than mine
